machines.name: OTTO-CHARGE ARM
summary: A 6-axis robot arm at each fast charger.
It finds the charge port, pushes the DC connector in and locks it.
It lets go when the charge ends. The car cannot move until the arm is home.
owner: A robot arm plugs your car in and unplugs it. No person handles the cable.
The arm measures the force on every move. A small error cannot jam the connector.
Your car cannot move until the arm is home.

facts.label: Connectors
facts.value: CCS1 (SAE J1772 combo) and NACS (SAE J3400), liquid-cooled

facts.label: Charge current
facts.value: 500 A DC, 1000 V, liquid-cooled at the connector

facts.label: Time to connect
facts.value: 18.5 s of arm motion

facts.label: Time to release
facts.value: 11.5 s of arm motion

facts.label: Finds the port
facts.value: Stereo cameras and a time-of-flight sensor find the inlet. A light ring helps at night.

facts.label: Force control
facts.value: A 6-axis force and torque sensor reads the insertion force. A compliance unit lets the head float up to 6 mm and 3 degrees. A small error cannot jam it.

facts.label: Latch
facts.value: A solenoid latch locks the connector in the inlet for the charge.

facts.label: Power path
facts.value: The charge current runs inside the arm. In each hollow link 2 copper bars carry it, one a pole. Nothing live is in the open. At the base, the shoulder and the elbow a booted link of braided copper joins 2 terminal boxes. It bends as the joint turns.

facts.label: Status lights
facts.value: Light rings on the arm show its state: teal ready, amber moving, green charging, red fault.

safety: A safety laser scanner on the riser watches the stall at knee height. A person in its field stops the arm.
An emergency stop on the riser cuts motor power (safe torque off).
OTTO-Q does not move a car while an arm is connected to it.
When a charger has a fault, the arm lets the car go at once. OTTO-Q sends the car to another charger.

machines.name: OTTO-CLEAN ARM
summary: An overhead arm over each fast charger. It vacuums the cabin while the car charges.
It swings in a plane 1.8 m above the roof. Only the wand goes into the car, and only through a door.
The doors open. The arm cleans one side, then the other side. Then the doors close.
owner: An overhead arm vacuums the cabin of your car while it charges.
Only the wand goes into the car, and only through an open door.
Every part of the arm keeps 0.10 m off the bodywork and the open doors.
Your car stays at its charger until the arm is home.

facts.label: Nozzle head
facts.value: Cleans the floor, the benches and the seat backs with vacuum, an air knife and a brush lip.

facts.label: Time for a clean
facts.value: About 6 min: 2.5 min on each side, and the moves between. The twin sets the time.

facts.label: Reach
facts.value: The wand reaches 1.37 m into the cabin.

facts.label: Mast
facts.value: Lowers the wrist from 2.18 m to 0.58 m above grade, beside the car, never over it.

facts.label: Clearance
facts.value: 0.10 m off the car and the open doors, at every point of the cycle.

facts.label: Vacuum supply
facts.value: A central vacuum producer on each canopy (about 3 kW per working arm, 30 kPa class) serves its arms.

facts.label: Crew
facts.value: The arm needs no technician.

facts.label: Status lights
facts.value: Lights on the base, the mast and the nozzle show the arm state.

safety: The arm swings above the roof. Nothing stands where a car drives.
The car stays on its stall until the arm is home.
A brake holds the mast when power is off.
A charger fault lets the car go at once. The arm at the next charger does the clean.

machines.name: OTTO-WASH
summary: A touchless wash line in each wash bay. The car stands still and the machines move round it.
A gantry makes 6 passes: pre-soak, 2 water-jet passes, rinse, 2 dry passes. Then it stows at the entrance.
Then 2 six-axis arms come from the exit end, one each side, and polish each sensor with a soft pad.
No brush touches the car. The doors stay shut.
owner: A machine washes your car in the wash bay. No brush touches the car.
It moves over the parked car 6 times: pre-soak, 2 water-jet passes, rinse and 2 dry passes.
The machine then stows at the entrance. 2 robot arms come down their tracks, one each side of the car.
They polish each camera, lidar and radar cover with a soft pad. The doors stay shut.

steps.label: The car stops at the bay centre
Hold for the cabin clean. The doors stay shut
steps.note: a detail seat only. The twin sets the time

steps.label: Pass 6: dry. The gantry stows at the entrance
The detail arms leave their docks
The detail arms go back to their docks
All stowed. The light turns green

facts.label: Passes
facts.value: 6 passes in about 3 min: pre-soak, 2 water-jet passes, rinse, 2 dry passes.

facts.label: Touch
facts.value: No brush. Only the soft pads touch the car, and only on its sensors.

facts.label: Sensor polish
facts.value: A soft pad on a floating, force-sensing head polishes each camera, lidar and radar cover. The 2 arms do 24 places in about 2.4 min.

facts.label: Detail arms
facts.value: 2 six-axis arms, one each side of the car. Points the pad square onto a sensor at any angle, as a hand does. The 3 wrist axes meet at one point. So the pad turns about that point and stays on the sensor.

facts.label: Pad
facts.value: The pad is microfibre over soft foam, 120 mm across. It is small enough for the edge of a roof lidar. J6 turns the pad a quarter turn each way to polish. It does not spin free, so no cable winds up.

facts.label: Push
facts.value: A 6-axis force sensor reads the push. The arm holds it at 5 N and stops at 10 N. A floating joint lets the pad tilt 6 degrees and give 8 mm. So it lies flat on a curved cover.

facts.label: Finds each sensor
facts.value: A camera beside the pad finds each sensor. A nozzle mists it with pure water first. No chemical is used.

facts.label: Arm tracks
facts.value: A floor track each side of the car takes a detail arm to any place along the car. Travel: 8.28 m.

facts.label: Pad care
facts.value: Each arm parks at the exit end, folded along its track, with its pad in a rinse cup. A nozzle in the cup rinses the pad with pure water after each car. The pad turns in the cup to throw the water off.

facts.label: Doors
facts.value: The doors stay shut in the wash bay. The cabin is cleaned at the fast charger.

facts.label: Spray arch
facts.value: Sprays the pre-soak, the wash water jets and the clear-water rinse. 9 flat-fan nozzles each side and 5 across the top.

facts.label: Air knives
facts.value: Blow the water off in the last 2 passes. Blowers: top 4 kW, sides 2 x 3 kW (class).

facts.label: Travel speed
facts.value: about 10 m/min

facts.label: Stop light
facts.value: A stop light faces the arriving car: red while the program runs, green when the car may go.

facts.label: Supply
facts.value: A drag chain brings power, water, chemicals and air. It lies in a covered trench in the floor, inboard of the west rail.

facts.label: Clear height
facts.value: 3.30 m under the beam

safety: Retracted, everything clears a car by more than 0.48 m.
The machine never moves over the car with a tool still on it.
The gantry and the arms never work at the same time. Each waits at its own end of the bay.
The dock stands north of the gantry's travel, so a parked arm is never under the gantry.
An arm stops its push at 10 N. If a wash ends early, each pad backs straight off the car.
No joint of an arm is hurried, even when a wash ends early.
A stop at each rail end holds a wheel if the machine runs past its travel.
The car leaves only when the light is green.
